title: Understanding the Sous Chef Salary: From Hourly Rates to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to calculate a sous chef salary from hourly rates under the Hospitality Award, including tax, super, and casual loading. Use our timesheet and pay guides.
salarySummary: A sous chef under the Hospitality Industry Award (Level 4) earns at least $32.45 per hour under the loaded rate arrangement for full-time Monday to Friday, equating to approximately $67,500 per year based on 38 hours per week.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for a sous chef in Australia?
faqs.a: The minimum hourly rate depends on the classification under the Hospitality Industry (General) Award 2020. A sous chef is typically classified at Level 4 or 5. Under the loaded rate arrangement for full-time Monday to Friday, Level 4 pays $32.45 per hour and Level 5 pays $34.49 per hour as of 1 July 2026. Standard rates without the loaded arrangement may differ. Always check the specific award classification and any applicable allowances.

faqs.q: How is casual loading applied to a sous chef hourly rate?
faqs.a: Casual employees under the Hospitality Award receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. For example, if the base rate for a Level 4 sous chef is $32.45 per hour, the casual rate would be $40.56 per hour. This loading is intended to compensate for the lack of paid leave and other entitlements. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how to apply it correctly.

faqs.q: Does the annual salary estimate include superannuation?
faqs.a: No, the annual salary estimate from an hourly rate does not include superannuation. Under the Super Guarantee, employers must pay 12% of ordinary earnings on top of the employee's base salary, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026–27). For example, a sous chef earning $67,500 per year would receive an additional $8,100 in super, making total remuneration $75,600. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) guide for more details.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the sous chef salary: from hourly rates to annual pay

If you're a sous chef or an employer in the hospitality industry, knowing how to convert an hourly rate into an annual salary is essential for budgeting, negotiating, and compliance. This article explains the process using the latest award rates from the Fair Work Ombudsman, the National Minimum Wage, and the Australian Taxation Office's 2026–27 tax scales. We'll focus on the **sous chef salary** under the Hospitality Industry (General) Award 2020, but the method applies to any hourly-paid role.

### How to convert an hourly rate to an annual salary

The basic formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time employee, we assume 38 ordinary hours per week (the standard under the National Employment Standards). If you work more or fewer hours, adjust accordingly. For example, a sous chef earning $32.45 per hour (the Level 4 loaded rate) working 38 hours per week would have an annual salary of:

$32.45 × 38 × 52 = $64,121.20

But note: the loaded rate arrangement in the award is based on a maximum 40‑hour week for Monday to Friday only. If your sous chef works weekends or nights, penalty rates apply separately. Always check the specific award provisions. Our [the timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and see the annual, fortnightly, and weekly equivalents instantly.

### Award rates for sous chefs under the Hospitality Industry Award

The Hospitality Industry (General) Award 2020 covers most sous chefs in hotels, restaurants, and catering. The classification depends on skill level and duties. A sous chef is typically a Level 4 or Level 5 employee. According to the Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guide effective from 1 July 2026, the loaded all‑purpose rates for full‑time Monday to Friday are:

- Level 3: $30.85 per hour
- Level 4: $32.45 per hour
- Level 5: $34.49 per hour
- Level 6: $35.41 per hour

These rates already include a loading that covers penalty rates for ordinary hours Monday to Friday. If your sous chef works outside those hours (e.g., weekends, nights, public holidays), additional penalties apply. The award also provides standard hourly rates for lower classifications (e.g., Level 2 cook grade 1 at $27.08 per hour). For a precise classification, refer to the award or use the Fair Work Commission's Modern Awards Pay Database.

For a sous chef working 38 hours per week at the Level 4 loaded rate, the annual salary would be approximately $64,121. However, many sous chefs work 40 hours or more, so the actual annual figure could be higher. The fortnightly pay would be $32.45 × 76 hours = $2,466.20 before tax.

### The National Minimum Wage and casual loading

Not all hospitality workers are covered by an award. If a sous chef is award‑free, the National Minimum Wage applies. From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour for a 38‑hour week ($1,004.90 per week). Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top, making the casual minimum rate $33.05 per hour.

For a casual sous chef under the award, the casual loading is already included in the casual rates shown in the pay guide. For example, a casual Level 2 cook grade 1 earns $33.85 per hour (including loading). Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how to apply the loading correctly if you're using a base rate.

### Tax and superannuation considerations

The annual salary figure from the formula is gross income before tax and super. The Australian Taxation Office's 2026–27 resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income between $18,201 and $45,000
- 30% on income between $45,001 and $135,000
- 37% on income between $135,001 and $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a 2% Medicare levy (using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). For a sous chef earning $64,121 per year, the estimated tax would be approximately $11,167 plus Medicare, leaving a take‑home pay of around $51,700. Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator can give you a more precise estimate.

Superannuation is paid on top of the salary. The Super Guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a $64,121 salary, the employer would contribute an additional $7,694.50 to super. This is not deducted from the employee's pay. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) guide for details.

### Using our timesheet and pay guides

To quickly convert any hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, or weekly figures, use our [the timesheet](/) tool. It lets you enter a base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading. The results show gross pay, estimated tax, Medicare, and super. For award‑specific rates, visit our [pay guides](/blog) page, which links to the latest Fair Work Ombudsman summaries. You can also explore [reference tables](/data) for industry averages and [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) updates.

Remember: the annual estimate assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates or allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Always consult the relevant award or employment contract for your exact entitlements. The Fair Work Ombudsman and Fair Work Commission are the authoritative sources for minimum rates and conditions.
